# The row that actually failed CI on luthersystems/elps PR #310
# (actions/runs/31222414614), verbatim.
#
# Reported as a false positive on the grounds that "no timing delta exceeds 15%"
# -- true, the worst was +6.37% -- and that the only magnitudes above 5% were in
# the B/s throughput column. But the run ALSO contained this, in the lisp
# package's B/op table:
#
#     EnvFunCallRecursion-4   3.768Mi -> 4.086Mi   +8.44% (p=0.008 n=5)
#
# That is an allocation metric at 8.44%, above the 5% allocation gate, and it is
# what fired. It is a TRUE positive:
#
#   * allocs/op for the same benchmark is IDENTICAL (40.08k, +0.00%) -- the
#     allocation COUNT did not move, only the bytes. Same allocations, bigger.
#   * the PR adds a `TailIterations int` field to CallFrame (lisp/stack.go),
#     which is allocated per call. 40,080 allocations x 8 bytes ~ 313 KiB;
#     the observed delta is 4.086Mi - 3.768Mi = ~325 KiB. The arithmetic lands.
#   * p=0.008 on the metric class that is near-deterministic in elps.
#
# So the gate correctly priced a real memory cost of the change. The fixture
# exists so that stays pinned: if a future edit stops this firing, the gate has
# lost the one signal it is most reliable at.
goos: linux
goarch: amd64
pkg: github.com/luthersystems/elps/lisp
cpu: AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor
